The test asserts on `caughtExceptions` immediately after `deletedAll.set(true)` without joining the reader thread, so a read that is still in flight when the deletions finish can append its exception after the assertion, letting the test pass even when the NPE regression it targets occurs (false negative). The reader thread is also left running (non-daemon, never joined), so it can continue issuing admin calls into subsequent tests. Fix: after setting `deletedAll` and before asserting, join the reader thread (e.g. store the Thread and call `thread.join(...)`), and make it a daemon thread so a failure in `remove()` cannot leak a spinning thread.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.texto: WHAT: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when destinationCalendar is null/empty, and the next line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. WHY: Callers frequently pass `destinationCalendar: []` or `null` (booking reminder cron, stripe/paypal webhooks, cancel/reschedule handlers, handleNewBooking). If such an event's location is Google Meet (MeetLocationType), this throws a TypeError and aborts event creation — the previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and fell back to Cal Video. HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

WHAT: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares `cal.externalId` against `externalCalendarId` itself inside the falsy branch, so the predicate can never be true and the find always returns undefined. WHY: When `externalCalendarId` is not provided the update no longer targets the booking's destination calendar (old behavior `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`); `calendarId` becomes undefined and the update runs against the wrong/default calendar or fails. HOW: fall back to the destination calendar's externalId (e.g. the first matching entry by credential or `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`).

WHAT: Same self-referential predicate `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` here always returns undefined when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. WHY: `calendarId` then falls back to `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, so delete targets the primary calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar — the event is not deleted (or the wrong event/calendar is targeted). HOW: fall back to the actual destination calendar id (e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`) instead of re-comparing externalCalendarId.

WHAT: The changed line now allows `selectedCalendar` to be undefined (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`), but the later conference-data `calendar.events.patch` call still passes the raw `selectedCalendar` as `calendarId`. WHY: When `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` is empty (common), the insert succeeds on "primary" but the follow-up patch is sent with an undefined calendarId, so the Google Meet hangout link patch fails/targets the wrong calendar. HOW: pass `selectedCalendar || "primary"` (or a resolved variable) to the patch call as well.

WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (set at line 1063-1067 when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar). WHY: For a COLLECTIVE event where only the non-organizer hosts have destination calendars, `teamDestinationCalendars` is populated but never attached, so those hosts are not invited — the exact scenario the PR aims to fix. HOW: initialize `destinationCalendar` to an empty array (instead of `null`) before pushing, e.g. `destinationCalendar: ... : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : []`.

WHAT: The guard for including the organization `slug` was inverted during the refactor — `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. WHY: `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` adds `slug` when team billing is DISABLED, while the new ternary adds it when billing is ENABLED, so organizations created with billing disabled no longer get a slug and organizations with billing enabled now incorrectly do (the sibling `requestedSlug` line 153 was left semantically unchanged). HOW: restore the original semantics, e.g. `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {} : { slug })` (or revert to `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`).

WHAT: The non-calendar branch of `referencesToCreate` now hardcodes `credentialId: undefined` (`credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`) where it previously used `result.credentialId`. WHY: video results produced by `createMeeting` (packages/core/videoClient.ts:78) carry `credentialId: credential.id`, and these references are persisted via `referencesToCreate` (handleNewBooking.ts:2121/2369); the cancellation path in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:491 only calls `deleteMeeting` when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy, so video meetings created by new bookings will no longer be deleted on cancel. HOW: use the result's credentialId for non-calendar results as well, e.g. `credentialId: result.credentialId` (drop the ternary).

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.texto: WHAT: totalPages computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which adds a phantom page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1). WHY: currentPage is computed correctly with floor(offset/limit)+1, so at the boundary the two disagree; 'next' stays enabled past the last real page and the user is sent to an empty page (offset clamped to user_count returns zero members). HOW: use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and return 0 when user_count is 0).

WHAT: add_members calls `group.add(user)` for every submitted username without filtering out users who are already members. WHY: `Group#add` (group.rb:272) does `self.users.push(user)`, which builds a new group_users join row unconditionally; GroupUser has no uniqueness validation, only a DB UNIQUE index on (group_id, user_id) (group_user.rb:18), so re-adding an existing member attempts a duplicate insert and the subsequent `group.save` fails/raises, turning the whole request into an error and preventing the other (valid) additions from persisting. The previous `usernames=` setter avoided this by computing `additions = expected - current` first. HOW: skip users already in the group before adding, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)` (or use the existing `usernames=` diff logic).

WHAT: `add_members` (and identically `remove_member` at line 85) read the group via `params.require(:group_id)`, but the new routes `put "members"`/`delete "members"` declared inside `resources :groups` (config/routes.rb:49-50) generate a member route `/admin/groups/:id/members` whose dynamic segment is `:id`, not `:group_id`. WHY: `params[:group_id]` is always nil on these requests, so `params.require(:group_id)` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400 — adding/removing a group member from the admin UI can never succeed; the controller specs don't catch this because they pass `group_id:` directly and bypass routing. HOW: use `params.require(:id)` in both `add_members` and `remove_member` (consistent with `update`, which uses `params[:id]` for the same resource).

fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.texto: WHAT: PasswordForm.authenticate now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) whenever isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, i.e. for the user merely named by an unauthenticated username submission (the username typed on the prior username-only step, or on the combined form), and fillContextForm for an identified user sets ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS, which causes the new authn_select form (passkeys.ftl) to render the user's credential IDs (authn_use_chk). WHY: an attacker can submit an arbitrary username and observe whether the passkey block/credential IDs appear, disclosing whether that account has a registered passkey (user enumeration) and its WebAuthn credential IDs before any credential is verified — the same broadened condition is reached via UsernamePasswordForm.challenge (UsernamePasswordForm.java:137-140). HOW: only emit the conditional-UI/authenticators block when the current request corresponds to a genuine re-authentication (e.g. gate on isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context) / the existing USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note) instead of any resolved context.getUser(), so passkey data is not exposed for a user identified only from an unverified username.

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.texto: WHAT: The mismatch check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without guarding for a missing `sender` key. WHY: `build_integration` only writes `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (lines 376-377), and the codebase elsewhere explicitly guards this field (`installation.py:44` does `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`), so an existing active GitHub integration whose metadata lacks `sender` (pipeline-created or legacy orphan integration without an OrganizationIntegration) reaches this line and raises KeyError, producing an HTTP 500 instead of the intended `error()` response. HOW: Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing sender as a validation failure (return `error(...)`).

WHAT: The OAuth `state` parameter is set to `pipeline.signature` and validated with `!= pipeline.signature`, but `pipeline.signature` is `md5_text(*pipe_ids)` computed only from pipeline view class names (pipeline/base.py:133) — a deterministic, publicly computable constant, not a per-session random value. WHY: The `state` check is supposed to prevent OAuth CSRF (an attacker binding their own authorization code to a victim's pipeline/session), but because the attacker can compute the signature it provides no protection and the callback accepts any state equal to the constant. HOW: Generate a per-pipeline random `state` (e.g. `secrets.token_urlsafe()`) at the start of the authorize step, store it in pipeline state, and compare the callback's `state` against that stored value.

WHAT: The OAuth exchange network calls are not wrapped in error handling — `safe_urlopen(...)` at line 423 and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` at line 434 (which calls `resp.raise_for_status()`) can raise, while only the subsequent body read/parse is inside a try/except. WHY: A GitHub connection timeout, 5xx, or non-200 from `/login/oauth/access_token` or `/user` propagates an unhandled exception out of `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, yielding a 500 error page instead of the graceful `error(request, ...)` failure path the code clearly intends (as shown for the missing-token case at 431-432). HOW: wrap the `safe_urlopen`/`get_user_info` calls in the same try/except (or catch `requests.RequestException`/`HTTPError`) and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

implement-access-token-context-encoding-.texto: WHAT: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time on grantType instead of validating rawTokenId. WHY: rawTokenId is never null-checked, so a null raw id is silently accepted and encodeTokenId then produces a corrupt id ending in ':null' (and the error message is misleading). HOW: change line 73 to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");

WHAT: isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) and then returns false when it equals expectedGrantShortcut (the condition is inverted). WHY: the encoded id is '<session><token><grant>:<uuid>' so the grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6); the wrong offset never matches, and even if it did, the inverted equals means the matcher never enforces the grant shortcut, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken/device tests pass regardless of the actual grant type and provide no coverage of the new encoding. HOW: use items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) and return false when it does NOT equal (i.e. `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`).
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId has inverted equals and substring(3,5) vs (4,6).

notification-rule-processing-engine-graf.texto: WHAT: The grafana branch of the rules.map lost its `key` prop — the diff removed `key={key}` from the rendered element, while the sibling `datasource` and `default` branches still pass `key={key}`. WHY: These elements are returned from an array map, so React falls back to index-based keys and logs a "missing key" warning; on filter/page updates items can be reused against the wrong rule state (stale DOM/state) because the stable artificial key that `KeyedRuleWithOrigin.key` was created for is no longer supplied. HOW: restore `key={key}` on the `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` element.

WHAT: RuleActionsButtons is instantiated with only `promRule` and no `rulerRule`, but in RuleActionsButtons.V2 the Silence drawer is gated by `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer` where `rule` is the (now always undefined) rulerRule prop. WHY: The new grafana-prom ability path enables the Silence menu item (canSilence true for folder-permitted users), so the item renders and `handleSilence` sets showSilenceDrawer=true, but the drawer never mounts — clicking Silence does nothing in the list view. HOW: gate the drawer on promRule too (e.g. render SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when the prom rule is a grafana alerting rule) or thread the needed identity through props instead of relying on rulerRule.

WHAT: `isFederated` was hardcoded to `false` (with a TODO) replacing the previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, so `immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided` no longer accounts for federated rule groups. WHY: useAllRulerRuleAbilities now also backs the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities / all useAlertRuleAbility call sites, so federated (Mimir) rules lose their immutability guard and get Update/Delete/Pause abilities that Grafana cannot actually perform, surfacing action buttons that error on click. HOW: preserve federated detection — pass the group/CombinedRule (or its group) into useAllRulerRuleAbilities and keep `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)` in the immutable calculation.

WHAT: When `skipToken` (or undefined) is passed, useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities sets `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`, which is `AlwaysSupported=true` because the undefined rule path returns loading=false; Duplicate/View therefore yield a supported ability [true, ...] instead of [false, false]. WHY: AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken for non-grafana (cloud/Mimir) rules and OR-s the result into `canDuplicate`, so a user holding only the Grafana AlertingRuleCreate permission can get a Duplicate action on an external rule they cannot create/duplicate. HOW: make the skip/undefined case explicitly unsupported (e.g. early-return all-[NotSupported, false] abilities when rule is undefined) rather than treating it as AlwaysSupported.

WHAT: The new `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)` computes a grafana-prom-rule delete ability, but the Delete menu item is still rendered only under `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165).
WHY: In the alert list view this PR targets, `rulerRule` is always undefined (RuleActionsButtons.V2 is invoked from GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47 with only `promRule`, and FilterView.tsx:157 passes no ruler rule), so the grafana delete branch can never produce a Delete menu item — Delete silently vanishes from the list view and the added ability is dead code. `handleDelete` was deliberately reworked to `() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)` so the action is intended to work from the identifier alone.
HOW: Change the gate to `canDelete && (rulerRule || promRule)` (or drop the `rulerRule` requirement and pass the identifier through), matching the existing rule viewer behavior.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.texto: WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object `{ success, data }`, but its result is assigned to `key` and persisted directly (`data: { key }`), instead of the parsed credential object that `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` used to return. WHY: this writes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` into `credential.key`; the very next instantiation calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) and now fails because scope/token_type/expiry_date/access_token/refresh_token are no longer at the top level, permanently breaking the Google Calendar credential after the first token refresh. HOW: use `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;` (or revert to `googleCredentialSchema.parse`).

WHAT: when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `Response` from `fetch`, but the caller reads `const token = res?.data`. WHY: a fetch `Response` has no `.data` property, so `token` is `undefined` and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError that is swallowed by the surrounding catch (only `invalid_grant` is re-thrown), so Google token refresh silently never happens while credential sharing is enabled. HOW: for the sharing branch, parse the response body (e.g. `await res.json()`) before reading `access_token`/`expiry_date`.

WHAT: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id into the parameter that represents the Cal.com *user* id. WHY: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to the credential-sync endpoint, so the self-hosted app store receives the credential id instead of the user id and will look up/refresh credentials for the wrong principal. HOW: thread the user id through (e.g. pass `credential.userId` from `biginAuth`) instead of `credentialId`.

WHAT: the added block refreshes the Salesforce access token and persists it, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` (line ~106) is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token`. WHY: the freshly fetched token is discarded for the connection created in this same call, so the immediate API request uses the (typically expired) old access token that triggered the refresh, defeating the refresh. HOW: assign the new token before constructing the connection (e.g. `accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`) and update `credentialKey` accordingly.

WHAT: in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the same string `"[object Object]"` (Zod types do not override `toString`), so the second property definition silently overwrites the first. WHY: the intended "any numeric property is the expiry" requirement (z.number) is never applied — the schema only enforces `access_token`, so malformed token responses without a numeric expiry pass validation and downstream `expiry_date` handling breaks. HOW: use a proper catch-all (e.g. `z.record(z.unknown())` combined with `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()`) or explicit fields rather than computed property keys.

WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` unconditionally sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the parsed response has no `refresh_token`.
WHY: `office365calendar` uses `refreshTokenResponseSchema` in which `refresh_token` is optional (CalendarService.ts:56) and then does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` (CalendarService.ts:264) before persisting. When the provider's refresh response omits `refresh_token`, this literal now overwrites the still-valid stored refresh token, so the next refresh attempt sends `refresh_token="refresh_token"` and permanently fails — the previous raw `safeParse` path preserved the old refresh token. HOW: only inject the placeholder when the caller's flow actually needs it (sharing/sync path), e.g. pass a flag or restrict the injection to the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` branch, and never overwrite an existing `refresh_token` in the non-sharing branch.

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.texto: Adding @include flexbox() to .small-action turns its .small-action-desc child into a shrink-to-fit flex item instead of the full-width block it was before. The edit/delete buttons inside .small-action-desc (styled `button { float: right }` at lines 306-310) and the avatar float are positioned relative to the desc's block width; with the desc no longer stretching across the 755px row (desktop/topic-post.scss:730), these floated controls no longer align to the right edge and the desc's width collapses to its content. Give .small-action-desc `flex: 1` (or `flex-grow: 1`) so it keeps filling the row, matching how .panel was handled with margin-left:auto in header.scss.

Making `.d-header .contents` a flex container turns `.extra-info-wrapper` into a flex item, and it has no `flex`/`min-width` set. WHY: previously `.extra-info-wrapper` was a full-width block so its child `.topic-link { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }` (desktop/topic-post.scss:532) truncated long topic titles; as a flex item with the default `min-width: auto`, its min-content size equals the full unbreakable title, so it cannot shrink and long titles no longer truncate (they overflow/clip the header). HOW: give `.extra-info-wrapper` (`@include order(2)` in common/base/topic.scss:30) `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;` so it can shrink and the ellipsis works again.

plugins-chore-renamed-instrumentation-mi.texto: WHAT: instrumentPluginRequest (and instrumentPluginRequestSize at lines 94-98) returns early with plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered from pluginTarget(ctx, pluginCtx.PluginID) without ever invoking the wrapped call m.next / fn, so the actual plugin request is never executed when the plugin is not found in the registry. WHY: a metrics-only concern now gates request execution — any request whose plugin is not resolvable (or whose ID is empty/unknown) is aborted and the caller receives ErrPluginNotRegistered instead of the plugin's real response/error, breaking request semantics for that path. HOW: resolve the target once and fall back to an "unknown" label value (still forward to m.next) instead of returning the lookup error, e.g. capture target via pluginTarget but proceed with fn(ctx) and only skip/annotate the metric when it is unavailable.

ref-crons-reorganize-incident-creation-i.texto: get_monitor_environment_context (lines 160-168) copies config into a local `config`, mutates it, then returns the unmodified `monitor_environment.monitor.config` — a real latent bug. It is byte-identical to the pre-existing code in mark_failed.py, and this PR does not change its behavior or reachability, so per scope it is not reported.

replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.texto: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature flag is enabled, the table branch renders <TableWidgetVisualization> with hardcoded empty props (columns={[]} and tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}) instead of the actual query results. Every dashboard/insights table widget for orgs with the flag will display a completely blank table, because result.data/result.meta/fields from the current iteration are discarded. Pass the real values, e.g. tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}} and the derived columns, matching what StyledSimpleTableChart receives (data={result.data}, metadata={result.meta}, fields).

get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() (which issues a Snuba get_events_snql query — models/group.py:305) plus recommended_event.get_environment() (a DB Environment.objects.get — eventstore/models.py:180) once per issue. It is invoked inside the per-issue loop in GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body (integration.py:406-410) and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body (integration.py:254-258), which iterate the top 5 issues, adding up to 5 extra Snuba queries and 5 DB lookups to every PR-comment workflow that previously performed no such lookups. Batch the environment resolution (e.g. resolve recommended events/environments for all issue ids in one query, or drop the per-issue lookup) so the comment workflow does not amplify its query count 6x.

fetch_error_details pairs error IDs with event payloads positionally: `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` then `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. get_multi does not preserve request order — it builds `{id: ...}` for uncached ids first and then `items.update(cache_items)`, so on a mix of cache hits/misses the returned dict is reordered (and deduplicated) relative to error_ids. The zip then attaches each `id` to another event's data, yielding ErrorEvents with a mismatched id. Iterate by id instead, e.g. `for event_id, data in events.items() if data is not None`, using the dict key as the id.

When organization.features includes 'use-table-widget-visualization', tableResultComponent renders <TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} /> with hardcoded empty data/columns, discarding result.data/result.meta. Every table widget shows an empty table under this flag. Pass the real result.data/result.meta and the derived columns (or the fieldHeaderMap/columns used by StyledSimpleTableChart).

get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() once per issue; it is invoked inside the per-issue list comprehension in both the GitHub and GitLab PRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body. get_recommended_event issues a Snuba get_events_snql query, so rendering a comment with N issues triggers N additional Snuba queries (N+1). Consider resolving recommended events in one batched query or skipping environment lookup when not needed.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.texto: The else branch treats a falsy scheduleSMS result as a send failure and increments retryCount, but scheduleSMS returns undefined when SMS sending is deliberately locked (twilioProvider.ts:92-95), not when it failed. WHY: for a user/team with SMS locked, the reminder gets retryCount=1 then 2, and the new deleteMany (retryCount > 1) deletes it on the next cron run, permanently dropping the SMS even though nothing failed and it should still send after unlocking. HOW: only increment retryCount for genuine failures; skip (do not increment) when the lock short-circuits, e.g. have scheduleSMS signal a locked/skipped result distinct from a falsy failure, or check the lock before calling and `continue`.

The catch block increments retryCount for every thrown error, not only SMS-send failures. WHY: checkSMSRateLimit() (twilioProvider.ts:98) throws when a user hits the monthly SMS rate limit, and errors from profile lookup / template building also land here, so a reminder that was never actually attempted (or merely rate-limited) is counted as a failed send and is deleted after two cron runs by the retryCount > 1 predicate. HOW: distinguish send failures from transient/setup errors, or only bump retryCount on Twilio send errors.

The second OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } is not scoped to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, unlike the first branch. WHY: it deletes any WorkflowReminder of any method with retryCount > 1; retryCount is a column shared by all reminder methods, so if any non-SMS path ever populates it the email/other reminders would be silently deleted by this SMS cron. HOW: add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the retryCount branch so the deletion stays limited to SMS reminders.

The new deleteMany branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` filters on a column that has no index (WorkflowReminder indexes are bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, and [method, scheduled, scheduledDate]). Because the OR combines an indexed branch (method+scheduledDate) with an unindexed one, Postgres cannot use a BitmapOr and must sequentially scan the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation, so cleanup cost grows linearly with the full table size. Add an index on retryCount (or on [scheduled, retryCount]) in the migration, or scope the delete to the same indexed columns (method + scheduled) so the planner can use an index.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.texto: The `--flusher-processes` click option defaults to 1, so the consumer always constructs SpanFlusher with max_processes=1. Combined with `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and `min(self.max_processes, ...)`, production always runs a single flusher process for all shards, making the intended per-shard fallback (`None` -> all shards) unreachable and the PR's parallelism inert unless operators explicitly override. Set the default to 0/None so the constructor's fallback (one process per shard) takes effect, or document that operators must pass the flag.

In join(), when a timeout is supplied and the deadline elapses on an early process, the loop `break`s, so every remaining process is neither waited on nor `terminate()`d. The previous implementation always ran `self.process.terminate()` after the wait. A hung process past the deadline is now leaked (only reaped at interpreter exit) instead of being killed. Continue iterating to terminate the remaining processes (or terminate all after the wait loop) rather than breaking out.

submit() now loops over all per-process buffers and calls `buffer.get_memory_info()`, and each call runs `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` which performs a full cluster-wide INFO scan (memory.py:82). With P flusher buffers this issues P identical cluster INFO queries per submit and sums the same node memories P times (ratio is unchanged but work is O(P)). Call `get_memory_info()` once and reuse it, instead of once per buffer.

Creating a separate `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process changes the meaning of `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments`. `flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(self.assigned_shards))` (buffer.py:382-384); since each process now holds only a subset of shards, shard_factor shrinks and the per-shard fetch cap grows, so the effective global per-cycle flush cap scales roughly with the number of flusher processes (and the `any_shard_at_limit` backpressure threshold becomes shard-count dependent). Divide the cap by the total number of shards (or the process count) so the documented global per-cycle limit and backpressure semantics are preserved.

WHAT: The restarted-path kill guard `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` is always False for the processes this class creates, because they come from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` (as the annotation on line 68 states), which is not a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process`.
WHY: When a flusher process crashes or hangs, `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement for the same shards while the previous process is never killed (`process.kill()` is skipped) and is never joined; for the hang case the stuck process is still alive and can resume flushing the same shards concurrently with its replacement, producing duplicate segments to buffered-segments. This is a regression: the pre-PR code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, which worked for these spawn processes.
HOW: Guard against the actual type, e.g. `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess): process.kill()` (or `hasattr(process, "kill")`), and/or compare against the same base class used to build it, so spawned processes are killed before replacement.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.texto: WHAT: Moving the lock from the whole BuildIndex function to only the `b.cache[key] = idx` write removes the mutual exclusion around index construction, so two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can now run simultaneously. WHY: BuildIndex is reachable concurrently for the same key (Search is a concurrent gRPC method calling getOrCreateIndex at search.go:148/160, and search.init builds keys in a parallel errgroup); both goroutines will call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk directory (bleve.go:96-98 when size > FileThreshold), flush, and then overwrite the cache, so the index instance returned to one caller is silently discarded and its writes are lost, plus a concurrent open/flush of the same bleve directory can corrupt it. The pre-existing TODO in getOrCreateIndex ("we want to block while building the index and return the same index for the key") shows this hazard was previously masked by the global lock. HOW: keep a per-key in-flight guard (e.g. a `sync.Map` of mutexes keyed by NamespacedResource, or singleflight) around the build so only the first caller builds and the rest reuse the cached index, while leaving the lock on the cache map write.

The new `s.log.Info(..., "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` call reads the bleve cache map without synchronizing with a concurrent writer. WHAT: `TotalDocs()` (bleve.go:144-154) iterates `b.cache` with no `cacheMu` lock, and it is invoked one line after search.go:207-213 starts the event-handler goroutine whose `handleEvent` → `getOrCreateIndex` → `build` → `BuildIndex` path writes `b.cache[key]` under `cacheMu.Lock()`. WHY: this is an unsynchronized concurrent map read and write, which the Go runtime handles as a fatal `concurrent map read and map write` that cannot be recovered and crashes the process. HOW: have `TotalDocs` hold `b.cacheMu.RLock()` while ranging over the map (or lock around the call), so the read cannot overlap the locked write.
